slot.brief: Sample activity measured at two instants; deduce half-life from the ratio and predict activity at a later time.

stem: The activity measurements for a radioactive sample are shown in the figure. Assuming exponential decay, choose the pair $(T_{1/2},A_{11})$, where $T_{1/2}$ is the half-life and $A_{11}$ is the activity at $t=11$ h.

verdicts.working: From 800 Bq at 2 h to 200 Bq at 8 h is a factor of 1/4 over 6 h, i.e. two half-lives; thus T₁/₂ = 3 h. Three hours after 8 h, the activity is 100 Bq.

working:
$\dfrac{A_8}{A_2}=\left(\dfrac12\right)^{(8-2)/T_{1/2}}=\dfrac14\Rightarrow T_{1/2}=3\ \text{h}$
$A_{11}=200\left(\dfrac12\right)^{(11-8)/3}=100\ \text{Bq}$

Independent check: From 800 Bq at 2 h to 200 Bq at 8 h is a factor of 1/4 over 6 h, i.e. two half-lives; thus T₁/₂ = 3 h. Three hours after 8 h, the activity is 100 Bq.
solution:
For exponential decay, $A(t)=A_0(1/2)^{t/T_{1/2}}$. From $A_2=800\,\text{Bq}$ and $A_8=200\,\text{Bq}$,
$$\frac{A_8}{A_2}=\left(\frac12\right)^{6/T_{1/2}}=\frac14\;\Rightarrow\;T_{1/2}=3\,\text{h}.$$
Thus $A_{11}=200(1/2)^{3/3}=100\,\text{Bq}$.

draft.stem: The activity measurements for a radioactive sample are shown in the figure. Assuming exponential decay, choose the pair $(T_{1/2},A_{11})$, where $T_{1/2}$ is the half-life and $A_{11}$ is the activity at $t=11$ h.

figure.description: Draw a horizontal time line with an arrow pointing right and three marked instants: t = 2 h, t = 8 h, and t = 11 h. Label the activity above the t = 2 h mark as 800 Bq and above the t = 8 h mark as 200 Bq. Leave the t = 11 h mark without an activity label.

A: Infers the half-life incorrectly from the activity ratio.
B: Applies two half-lives instead of one between 8 h and 11 h.
D: Treats a quarter of the activity as one half-life.
